literal: Yi's physical strength surpassed others; his bow drew nearly ten piculs; Duke of Chenliu Qian greatly praised his spear.
idiomatic: Yi's strength was unmatched; his bow drew near ten piculs; Qian of Chenliu marveled at his spear.

literal: People at the time said: "Wei Prince's bow, Huan Prince's spear."
idiomatic: Men said: "Wei Prince's bow, Huan Prince's spear."

literal: When Taiwu was first born, Daowu rejoiced and called Yi in at night, saying: "You hear a night summons—are you not afraid?"
idiomatic: Taiwu's birth pleased Daowu; he summoned Yi at night: "Called at night—are you afraid?"

literal: Yi said: "Wonder, yes; fear, none."
idiomatic: Yi said: "I wonder, but I do not fear."

literal: The emperor told him Yi Taiwu was born and gave Yi imperial horses, belt, brocade, and the like.
idiomatic: Daowu told him of Taiwu's birth and gave him imperial horses, belt, and silks.

literal: Earlier Marquis of Shanggu Ji, Zhang Gun, Xu Qian of Dai Commandery, and others were famed in the day and had first entered the army.
idiomatic: Ji of Shanggu, Zhang Gun, Xu Qian of Dai, and others were famed when they first joined the army.

literal: Hearing Yi treated scholars well, they went to Yi first; Yi received them all with courtesy and together discussed affairs of the age.
idiomatic: Hearing Yi honored talent, they sought him first; he welcomed them and talked of the times.

literal: Qian and the other three said: "Duke of Pingyuan has great talent and unworldly plans—we should cling to his tail."
idiomatic: The three said: "Pingyuan has great gifts and rare design—we should follow him."

literal: Daowu, for Yi's capacity and standing, treated him especially heavily, often visiting his residence with family courtesy.
idiomatic: Daowu valued Yi's stature, favored him deeply, and visited his home like kin.

literal: Yi, proud of merit and trusting favor, then with Duke of Yidu Mu Chong lay in ambush plotting rebellion.
idiomatic: Proud of merit and grace, Yi with Mu Chong of Yidu hid armed men to rebel.

literal: Chong's son Zhuliu was among the hidden men; Daowu summoned him, about to give a mission.
idiomatic: Chong's son Zhuliu lay among them; Daowu called him to assign a task.

literal: Zhuliu, hearing the summons, feared exposure, climbed the wall and reported; the emperor kept it secret and forgave him.
idiomatic: Zhuliu, afraid, went over the wall and told; the emperor hid the matter and pardoned him.

literal: In the sixth year of Tiansi the heavens changed often; diviners said: "A rebellious minister will lie dead, blood on the ground."
idiomatic: In Tiansi year six the sky was strange; diviners said a traitor would die in blood.

literal: The emperor hated this and killed many nobles, wishing to appease heaven's disaster.
idiomatic: Daowu loathed the omen and killed many lords to satisfy heaven.

literal: Yi was uneasy within and fled alone on horseback.
idiomatic: Uneasy, Yi fled alone on horseback.

literal: The emperor sent men to seize him and granted death; he was buried with commoner rites.
idiomatic: Men seized him; he was ordered to die and buried as a commoner.

literal: Yi had fifteen sons.
idiomatic: Yi had fifteen sons.

literal: Zuan, five years old, Daowu ordered him raised in the palace with the same favor as the imperial sons.
idiomatic: Zuan, five, was raised in the palace like an imperial son.

literal: When Taiwu succeeded he was made Inspector of Dingzhou, enfeoffed Duke of Zhongshan, advanced to prince, and given a hand-drawn carriage as special honor.
idiomatic: Taiwu made him inspector of Dingzhou, Duke of Zhongshan, then prince, with a hand-drawn carriage as favor.

literal: Zuan loved wine and favored flatterers; government was bought with bribes.
idiomatic: Zuan drank and loved sycophants; office went to the highest bidder.

literal: Taiwu killed his favorite intimates.
idiomatic: Taiwu executed his favorites.

literal: Later, repenting, he became careful and was made Grand General of the Inner Palace.
idiomatic: Repenting, he grew careful and became grand general of the inner palace.

literal: In office he was frugal and cautious and was again praised as honest and fair.
idiomatic: In office he was spare and cautious and was called honest again.

literal: Zuan was eldest in the clan; when the imperial house had affairs, all consulted him.
idiomatic: Eldest of the line, the clan sought him on family matters.

literal: He died; posthumous name Jian.
idiomatic: He died; posthumous name Jian.

literal: Zuan's younger brother Liang was loyal and steadfast by nature.
idiomatic: His brother Liang was loyal by nature.

literal: Mingyuan recorded Yi's merit and enfeoffed Liang Prince of Nanyang to continue Yi's line.
idiomatic: Mingyuan honored Yi's service and made Liang Prince of Nanyang to continue the line.

literal: His son Zhen had courage beyond others.
idiomatic: His son Zhen had uncommon daring.

literal: Under Taiwu he was Director of Palace Guards.
idiomatic: Under Taiwu he was director of palace guards.

literal: On campaign against the Rouran he suddenly met a detached enemy band, too many to fight.
idiomatic: Against the Rouran he met a sudden enemy detachment too large to fight.

literal: Zhen dismounted on the mountain, loosed saddle and horses to show an ambush; the enemy suspected it and withdrew.
idiomatic: He loosed horses on a hill as if ambushed; the enemy feared and left.

literal: At the start of Xiaowen he was enfeoffed Duke of Pei and later made Inspector of Southern Yu.
idiomatic: Early in Xiaowen's reign he was Duke of Pei, later inspector of Southern Yu.

literal: When Mountain Hu of Dahu raided, earlier governors had only restrained them.
idiomatic: Dahu Mountain Hu raided; earlier governors had only held them loosely.

literal: Zhen summoned chiefs of Xincai and Xiangcheng barbarians and had them watch archery.
idiomatic: Zhen called chiefs of Xincai and Xiangcheng to watch shooting.

literal: He first chose more than twenty skilled archers at his side; Zhen shot several arrows himself, all hitting, then ordered his men to shoot in turn.
idiomatic: He picked twenty good archers; shot himself and hit, then had his men shoot in turn.

literal: First a condemned prisoner was brought to share the limit; ordered to miss, Zhen blamed and beheaded him at once.
idiomatic: A condemned man was made to shoot; told to miss, Zhen beheaded him on the spot.

literal: The barbarian chiefs submitted in awe, looking at one another with legs trembling.
idiomatic: Chiefs trembled and submitted in awe.

literal: He also had his men take ten condemned men, all dressed as barbarians, saying they were raiders.
idiomatic: He dressed ten condemned men as Hu raiders.

literal: Zhen sat in state, feigned to look at the sky; when the wind stirred slightly he told the barbarians: "The wind is a little violent; raiders seem to have entered—not more than ten, about fifty li southwest."
idiomatic: Feigning to read the sky he said: "Wind rises—perhaps ten raiders fifty li southwest."

literal: He at once sent horsemen to seize them; indeed ten were bound and sent in.
idiomatic: Horsemen seized them; ten were bound and brought.

literal: Zhen told the barbarians: "Your villages make thieves like this—should they not die?"
idiomatic: He said: "Thieves like this in your hills—should they not die?"

literal: The barbarians all kowtowed: "Ten thousand deaths are fitting."
idiomatic: They kowtowed: "They deserve ten thousand deaths."

literal: Zhen beheaded them at once.
idiomatic: He beheaded them immediately.

literal: " He comforted them and sent them back; from then on the border knew no violent raids.
idiomatic: He soothed them and sent them home; raids ceased.

literal: More than three thousand households of Huainan submitted together and were placed east of the city by the Ru River in a quarter called Guiyi.
idiomatic: Three thousand Huainan households submitted and were settled east of the Ru in Guiyi quarter.

literal: Earlier the magnate Hu Qiusheng of Yuzhou had often dealt with outsiders; when Zhen was inspector Qiusheng, once offending, bore hatred and plotted disorder, falsely announcing marriage to enter the city and saying: "The inspector means to move the great families of the city and send them to Dai."
idiomatic: Magnate Hu Qiusheng had trafficked with outsiders; offended by Zhen, he plotted, entered under a wedding pretext, and said the inspector would send the city's great houses to Dai.

literal: Together they plotted to turn the city.
idiomatic: They plotted to rebel and seize the city.

literal: Shi Daoqi of the city secretly told Zhen; he quickly seized Qiusheng and all conspirators.
idiomatic: Shi Daoqi reported secretly; Zhen seized Qiusheng and the plotters.

literal: Zhen said: "I do not fail others—why would they rebel?
idiomatic: Zhen said: "I have not failed them—why would they rebel?

literal: Only Qiusheng deceived them.
idiomatic: Only Qiusheng lied.

literal: If I seize at once the crowd will be greatly afraid; I will wait quietly—they will soon repent and submit."
idiomatic: A sudden arrest would panic them; I will wait—they will repent."

literal: Before the words ended three hundred men of the city bound themselves and came to the gate, stating Qiusheng's deceitful slander.
idiomatic: Before he finished, three hundred bound themselves at the gate and accused Qiusheng.

literal: Qiusheng fled alone on horseback; Zhen pardoned and did not pursue.
idiomatic: Qiusheng fled alone; Zhen let him go.

literal: Later he was summoned as Director of Pasturage of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: He was later recalled as Director of Pasturage.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: Posthumously made Palace Attendant and equal to the Three Excellencies; posthumous name Jian.
idiomatic: Posthumously Palace Attendant, equal to the Three Excellencies; posthumous name Jian.

literal: He had eight sons.
idiomatic: He had eight sons.

literal: The fifth son Rui.
idiomatic: The fifth son was Rui.

literal: Earlier Rui's mother Lady Yin, while pregnant, was injured; later she slept by day and dreamed an old man in cap and gown told her: "I give you a son—do not grieve."
idiomatic: Rui's mother Lady Yin, injured while pregnant, later dreamed an old man in robes said: "I grant you a son—do not worry."

literal: " Waking she rejoiced privately; she also asked diviners, who said: "Great fortune."
idiomatic: Waking, she rejoiced; diviners said: "Great fortune."

literal: " Before long Rui was born.
idiomatic: Soon Rui was born.

literal: Zhen thought it matched the dream and named him Rui, style Tiansi.
idiomatic: Zhen took it for the dream and named him Rui, style Tiansi.

literal: Office: Grand Master for the Palace.
idiomatic: He reached Grand Master for the Palace.

literal: Died; posthumously Minister of Ceremonies.
idiomatic: He died; posthumously Minister of Ceremonies.

literal: Yi's younger brother Lie was fierce and martial with plans.
idiomatic: Yi's brother Lie was fierce and clever.

literal: In Yuan Shao's revolt the hundred officials dared not speak; only Lie went out, pretended to join Shao, and offered to seize Mingyuan; Shao trusted him and he went out through Yanchun Gate.
idiomatic: In Shao's revolt officials were silent; Lie went out, feigned loyalty to Shao, offered to seize Mingyuan; Shao trusted him and he left by Yanchun Gate.

literal: He then welcomed and established Mingyuan.
idiomatic: He brought Mingyuan to the throne.

literal: For merit he was advanced to Prince of Yinping.
idiomatic: For merit he was made Prince of Yinping.

literal: Died; posthumous name Xi.
idiomatic: He died; posthumous name Xi.

literal: His son Qiu inherited.
idiomatic: His son Qiu succeeded.

literal: Younger brother Daozi, office: Junior Grandee.
idiomatic: Younger brother Daozi was junior grandee.

literal: Daozi's son Luo, office: Colonel of the Feathered Forest.
idiomatic: Daozi's son Luo was colonel of the feathered forest.

literal: Luo's son Qi, Attendant Censor.
idiomatic: Luo's son Qi was attendant censor.

literal: Qi's son Yan, at the start of Xiaojing was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Masters of Writing; impartial and unbending, praised by the age.
idiomatic: Qi's son Yan, early in Xiaojing, rose to Director of the Masters of Writing, fair and firm, praised in his day.

literal: Sent out as Inspector of Yingzhou; in office not long, the people relied on him with joy.
idiomatic: Made inspector of Yingzhou; the people soon trusted him.

literal: In Jiang Tianle's rebellion he was implicated; an edict had him sent to Dingzhou and granted death.
idiomatic: Implicated in Jiang Tianle's revolt, he was sent to Dingzhou and ordered to die.

literal: Yan loved collecting books; his family library held many secretariat volumes; all who borrowed were not refused, and he was praised for this too.
idiomatic: Yan collected books; his house held secretariat texts; he lent freely and was praised for it.

literal: Lie's younger brother Gu was brave and fierce with spirit.
idiomatic: Lie's brother Gu was bold and spirited.

literal: Young, with brother Yi he followed Daowu as guard at the side.
idiomatic: Young, he and Yi guarded Daowu.

literal: Sent to Murong Chui; in Chui's last years power lay with subordinates, so they detained Gu for a bribe; Daowu broke relations.
idiomatic: Sent to Murong Chui; late in Chui's reign they held Gu for ransom; Daowu cut ties.

literal: Gu led his men in flight; Chui's son Bao seized him; Chui treated him still more generously; he applied himself to learning and recited classics in hundreds of thousands of words; Chui's people all respected him.
idiomatic: Gu fled; Bao seized him; Chui treated him well; he studied classics by the hundred thousand words and was respected in Yan.

literal: When Daowu attacked Zhongshan, Murong Pulin then killed Gu to steady the hearts of the masses.
idiomatic: When Daowu attacked Zhongshan, Pulin killed Gu to bind the people.

literal: The emperor, hearing it, mourned deeply.
idiomatic: Daowu mourned deeply.

literal: When Zhongshan was pacified he opened Pulin's tomb, cut his corpse, seized those who had plotted against Gu—Fu Gaoba, Cheng Tong, and others—and exterminated five degrees of kin, killing them with great blades.
idiomatic: Zhongshan fell; he opened Pulin's tomb and cut the corpse; seized Fu Gaoba, Cheng Tong, and others who had harmed Gu, exterminated five degrees, and killed them with great blades.

literal: He buried Gu, posthumously Prince of Qin Min, and enfeoffed his son Kui Prince of Yuzhang to continue Gu.
idiomatic: He buried Gu as Qin Prince Min and made son Kui Prince of Yuzhang to continue him.

literal: Prince of Changshan Zun was Shoujiu's son.
idiomatic: Changshan Prince Zun was Shoujiu's son.

literal: Young and boldly brave, he did not bind himself to small rules.
idiomatic: Young, he was fierce and scorned small rules.

literal: At Daowu's beginning he had founding merit and was enfeoffed Duke of Lueyang.
idiomatic: At Daowu's rise he had founding merit and was Duke of Lueyang.

literal: When Murong Bao was defeated he separately led seven hundred horse and blocked his return, thereby winning the victory at Canhe.
idiomatic: When Bao was beaten he led seven hundred horse, blocked the retreat, and won Canhe.

literal: When Zhongshan was pacified he was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, added Palace Attendant, and held the mouth of Bohai.
idiomatic: Zhongshan pacified, he was left vice director, palace attendant, and held Bohai's mouth.

literal: When bandits rose in Boling and Bohai, Zun pacified them, was moved to regional inspector, and enfeoffed Prince of Changshan.
idiomatic: Bandits rose in Boling and Bohai; Zun pacified them, became inspector, and Prince of Changshan.

literal: Zun loved wine and women.
idiomatic: Zun loved wine and women.

literal: In the fourth year of Tiansi, for drunken disorder he lost propriety toward the Princess of Taiyuan.
idiomatic: In Tiansi year four, drunk, he insulted the Princess of Taiyuan.

literal: Granted death; buried with commoner rites.
idiomatic: He was ordered to die and buried as a commoner.

literal: His son Su was born of Mingyuan's wet nurse and was especially favored.
idiomatic: His son Su was born to Mingyuan's nurse and was specially loved.

literal: At Taiwu's beginning he again inherited the title.
idiomatic: Under Taiwu he inherited again.

literal: When Xiutu and Yuyuan rebelled, Su attacked, beheaded the chieftain, and moved more than a thousand households to the north of Zhuolu, establishing Pingyuan Commandery to settle them.
idiomatic: When Xiutu and Yuyuan rebelled, Su beheaded the chief and moved a thousand households north of Zhuolu, founding Pingyuan commandery.

literal: When Tongwan was pacified, because Su had prestige and a policy of winning hearts, he was made Acting Commander and Grand General Who Conquers the West to hold it.
idiomatic: Tongwan pacified, for his awe and winning ways he was acting commander and grand general conquering the west.

literal: Later he was made Grand Officer of the Inner Court.
idiomatic: He was later grand officer of the inner court.

literal: When Wencheng succeeded he pursued lenient government and abolished miscellaneous levies.
idiomatic: Wencheng pursued leniency and ended mixed levies.
